title: Paragraphs and pace 2
summary: Paragraphs with dates, times and links in them — the last awkward join, practised until it is not.
intro: This lesson mixes everything. The paragraphs carry times, dates, an address and a link, which means your hands leave the home row and come back several times a line. That join is the last thing in the course that is genuinely awkward, and the only cure is meeting it often enough that it stops being an event.
congrats: That is the last lesson. Everything after this is a drill on your own weak keys and the final test — three minutes of ordinary writing, which is now something you can do without thinking about your hands at all.

screens.content:
The class meets on Monday and Thursday at 18:30.
Each one runs for 45 minutes.
If you want a place, send an email before the 10th.
screens.text: Times and dates inside plain sentences. The colon is Shift and the semicolon, so your little finger barely moves for it.
The awkward pieces of that paragraph on their own — a time, a number, a weekday. These are what slowed you down, not the words.

screens.content:
There are 24 hours in a day and you will spend about 3 of them at a keyboard.
Over a year that is more than 1000 hours.
Typing twice as fast gives you back more time than almost anything else you could learn.
screens.text: Bigger numbers in longer sentences. Type each number as a single shape rather than as separate digits.

screens.content:
In the morning I get up at 6 and work for an hour before anyone writes to me.
I answer the mail first, then the harder things.
By 9 the day has usually decided what it wants to be.
screens.text: Ordinary writing with one number a line. Keep the rhythm even across the join — that is the whole exercise.
Longer words this time, no numbers. Let this one run fast; you have earned a screen where nothing is difficult.

screens.content:
Here is the address I promised: https://typingease.site/lessons
You can write to me at sam@mail.com whenever you like.
See you on Thursday!
screens.text: A link and an address inside a note. No spaces inside either of them, and the sentence carries on afterwards as though nothing happened.

screens.content:
After three months I type about 45 words a minute at 97 per cent.
I do not look at the keyboard any more, and I have stopped noticing that I am typing.
A page of writing now takes a few minutes instead of half an hour.
That was the whole reason I started.
screens.text: The last screen before the test. Enter at the end of every line, and no hurry — this one is worth typing properly.
